edit.description: `loopCompletionSummary`'s fold, where the `shipped ...` segment is nested inside the errored-ticks branch, and the doc comment above it that rosters what the line names
the exit-code/summary cases, including the errored-and-shipped one whose shipped segment moves
the two whole-summary `toBe` assertions over a real supervised run — the spend-only line and the errored-only line, each of which gains the yield segment

summary: The loop's completion summary names shipped tags only inside its errored-ticks branch, so a run that spent a full budget shipping nothing prints the same shape as one that shipped four entries

per.section: Exit codes — the run never lies to CI

acceptance: wherever `loopCompletionSummary` emits a line, that line names the run's yield: the `shipped ...` segment lifts out of the `erroredTicks.length > 0` branch into its own unconditional segment, with an explicit nothing-shipped spelling for an empty `shippedTags`, and the spend stays last. A run whose every tick was a `clean-exit` — no errors, a full budget of agent invocations — no longer prints byte-identically in shape to a productive run. A run with nothing at all to report still returns `undefined`; typecheck and suite green.
tests: the loop completion summary names the run's shipped tags on a run that errored no tick
the loop completion summary spells nothing shipped on a run whose summary is its spend alone
notes: Operator ruling (inbox, 2026-09-29): (b), and the code is short of the spec, not the spec wrong — the spend is reported "so what a run cost is read where its outcome is", and the outcome is what shipped. Not (c). Scoped to the literal reading: the summary, when emitted, names the yield, so the `parts.length === 0` `undefined` return stays and `tests/cliVerdict.test.ts:230` holds. Verified: `src/cliVerdict.ts:284` nests `shipped` in the errored branch.
